- `last_transition` is `transitions[-1]` or `None`. Its `.result` mirrors `last_action_result`; older transitions may have an empty `.result`. For before/after diffs, compare `last_transition.before_frame` to `last_transition.after_frame`; do not compare `current_frame` to `history[-1].frame`.
- `last_action_result` is the persisted result dict from the most recent `action(...)` call. It remains available across later Python inspection calls that do not call `action(...)`, and is `{}` before any action result exists. Read transition metadata from fields/keys such as `last_action_result['board_changed']`, `last_action_result['done']`, `last_action_result['level_completed']`, `last_action_result['game_over']`, `last_action_result['reward']`, and `last_action_result['valid_actions']`.
- `valid_actions` is the current list of valid action names.
- Call `action(actions)` to execute one or more real environment actions from Python.
- Pass `action(actions)` a list like `['LEFT']` or `[{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 7}]`.
- One action usually returns one frame, but a single action can result in a short multi-frame animation.
- After `action(actions)` returns, `current_frame`, `previous_frame`, `history`, `transitions`, `valid_actions`, and `last_action_result` are refreshed.
- Each result reports `board_changed`, plus `gameplay_changed` and `no_impact`: the harness learns the game's deterministic HUD/edge band (a moves-remaining or timer bar) online and tells you whether your action changed real gameplay (`gameplay_changed`) or only advanced that band (`no_impact` -- a wasted move, e.g. pressing into a wall). `hud_band` names the learned band when one exists (e.g. `rows 61-62`).
- `action(actions, intent=...)` defaults to `intent='explore'`: an explore action that turns out `no_impact` STOPS the rest of that batch (`stop_reason='no_impact_action'`) and returns so you re-ground, instead of wasting the queued actions on a plan the environment just disproved. Pass `intent='solve'` for a committed sequence you do not want interrupted by the no-impact check.
- Optional precision upgrade for that check: if you can pin down the deterministic HUD/bar exactly, write a PURE `advance_hud(frame, action) -> frame` (frame is the `.ascii` letter grid; return it with ONLY the bar advanced one step, everything else identical) and commit it in a `HUD model:` section with a fenced python code block. The harness re-verifies it against every action and, while its bar prediction holds, uses it (`no_impact_source: model`) instead of the statistical band -- you write it ONCE and it then runs free every turn with no further tokens. It only asks you to rewrite when it mispredicts (`hud_model: stale`, e.g. a refill or a new level). No HUD in this game? Don't write one -- the statistical fallback handles it (`no_impact_source: band` or `exact`).
- `ACTION7` is a valid game-specific action when it appears in `valid_actions`. Its meaning is not fixed across games; infer it from a safe probe and the returned before/after and animation metadata rather than assuming it means undo, confirm, or back.
- Every action in the result's `executed_actions` carries an `animation` record summarizing its intermediate frames (which are not visible in `current_frame`): `num_frames`, `changed`, `only_changed` (a transient flash that left the same final board), `total_cells_changed`, `cells_changed_per_frame` (per frame, where 0 is a held/dwell frame), and `objects` -- one string per connected animated region, e.g. `top-left (19,27) 4x4, 16 cells, per-frame [...]`, so two things moving at once (a box resizing while a light blinks) each keep a tight bounding box.
- Beyond the `animation` record above, two optional runtime variables expose the actual per-action frames: `last_animation` and `frame_stats`.
- `current_frame` is always the settled board after your last action -- on its own it is enough for a purely static reading, and you never have to look further.
- If you want to, `last_animation` additionally exposes every frame the engine produced for each INDIVIDUAL action of your most recent `action(...)` call: a list with one entry per action, in execution order, each with `.action` and `.frames` (intermediate animation frames plus the final frame; length 1 means that action caused no animation). After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.
- `show_animation_by_objects(action_index=0)` prints that action's animation one object at a time, each cropped to its own bounding box (labeled with the object's top-left row, col) and reduced to its distinct states -- small and legible even for a long animation. Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.
- `show_animation_by_bbox(action_index=0, row=..., col=..., rows=..., cols=...)` prints the same animation cropped to a region YOU choose (top-left `row`,`col` plus `rows`,`cols`) -- use it to inspect a spot the object split missed. Omit `rows`/`cols` to watch the FULL animation frames.
- It is entirely your judgement whether the intermediate frames are signal or noise. Motion may be meaningful (an object sliding, a chain reaction, a knock-on effect) OR incidental (a decorative transition, a flashing timer/HUD, a cosmetic redraw). Treat multi-frame motion as a HYPOTHESIS to test against the puzzle, not a fact. Reading `last_animation` costs tokens only when you inspect it, so pull it only when you expect it to help.

# Let's map the maze path as graph of nodes (white/gray tiles) adjacency.
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
# Build mapping id->color
id2col = {n['id']: n['color'] for n in nodes}
# Find path nodes: white W or gray g maybe.
path_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')]
print('path node count', len(path_ids))
# Find blue node id
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
# Build adjacency subgraph
path_adj = {}
for i,j in adj:
    if i in path_ids and j in path_ids:
        path_adj.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
        path_adj.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
# Also blue adjacent to path nodes?
blue_neighbors = [j for i,j in adj if i==blue_id] + [i for i,j in adj if j==blue_id]
print('blue neighbors', blue_neighbors)
# Determine current cell of blue in terms of which path node it overlaps?
# Blue may be sitting on top of path nodes, maybe it occupies multiple path cells.
# Let's inspect ascii around blue to see underlying pattern.
lines = current_frame.ascii.splitlines()
r_start, r_end = 14, 18
c_start, c_end = 18, 26
crop = []
for i in range(r_start, r_end):
    crop.append(''.join(lines[i][j] for j in range(c_start, c_end)))
print('\n'.join(crop))
# Let's find green location
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
green_neighbors = [j for i,j in adj if i==green_id] + [i for i,j in adj if j==green_id]
print('green neighbors', green_neighbors)
print('green neighbor colors', [id2col[n] for n in green_neighbors])

<parameter=code>

# Build full adjacency map for path nodes and try BFS from both candidate starts
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)

path_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9]
path_set = set(path_ids)

blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')

blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_set]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_set]

print('blue path neighbors', blue_neighbors)
print('green path neighbors', green_neighbors)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()
    queue=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        queue.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    found=None
    while queue:
        nid,d = queue.popleft()
        if nid==target_id:
            found=(nid,d,parent)
            break
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_set and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                queue.append((nb,d+1))
    return found

# try each green neighbor as target
for t in green_neighbors:
    res = bfs(blue_neighbors, t)
    if res:
        nid,d,parent = res
        print('found target', t, 'distance', d)
        # reconstruct
        cur=nid
        path=[]
        while cur is not None:
            path.append(cur)
            cur=parent.get(cur)
        path.reverse()
        print('path ids', path)
        break
else:
    print('no path found')

# We have path from blue start node 10 to green neighbor 59 via 32 steps (node moves).
# Need to translate node steps to cardinal moves (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT).
# For each consecutive node pair, compute bounding box movement.
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
path_ids = [10,14,22,26,27,28,23,15,16,17,24,29,31,39,38,37,36,35,45,48,49,50,51,52,57,63,64,65,58,53,54,55,59]
moves = []
for a,b in zip(path_ids, path_ids[1:]):
    na = id2node[a]
    nb = id2node[b]
    # get top-left
    def tl(n):
        bnd = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in bnd]
        cols = [p[1] for p in bnd]
        return min(rows), min(cols)
    ra, ca = tl(na)
    rb, cb = tl(nb)
    if rb > ra:
        moves.append('DOWN')
    elif rb < ra:
        moves.append('UP')
    elif cb > ca:
        moves.append('RIGHT')
    elif cb < ca:
        moves.append('LEFT')
    else:
        moves.append('?')
print('moves length', len(moves))
print(moves)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()

def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]

def bfs(start_ids, target_id):

seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']

    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
path_set = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9)
blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_set]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_set]

def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), min(cols)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()
    queue=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        queue.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while queue:
        nid,d = queue.popleft()
        if nid==target_id:
            return d,parent
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_set and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                queue.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

remaining_moves = []

    d,parent = bfs(blue_neighbors, t)
    if d is not None:
        cur = t

        for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):

            if rb>ra: remaining_moves.append('DOWN')

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Check current blue position and recompute remaining moves
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
path_set = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9)
blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_set]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_set]

def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), min(cols)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()
    queue=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        queue.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while queue:
        nid,d = queue.popleft()
        if nid==target_id:
            return d,parent
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_set and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                queue.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

remaining_moves = []
for t in green_neighbors:
    d,parent = bfs(blue_neighbors, t)
    if d is not None:
        cur = t
        path = []
        while cur is not None:
            path.append(cur)
            cur = parent.get(cur)
        path.reverse()
        for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
            ra,ca = tl(id2node[a])
            rb,cb = tl(id2node[b])
            if rb>ra: remaining_moves.append('DOWN')
            elif rb<ra: remaining_moves.append('UP')
            elif cb>ca: remaining_moves.append('RIGHT')
            elif cb<ca: remaining_moves.append('LEFT')
        print('remaining moves', remaining_moves)
        break
if remaining_moves:
    action(remaining_moves)
print('result', last_action_result.get('level_completed'), last_action_result.get('done'))

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Recompute remaining moves
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
path_set = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9)
blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_set]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_set]

def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), min(cols)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()
    queue=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        queue.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while queue:
        nid,d = queue.popleft()
        if nid==target_id:
            return d,parent
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_set and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                queue.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

remaining_moves = []
for t in green_neighbors:
    d,parent = bfs(blue_neighbors, t)
    if d is not None:
        cur = t
        path = []
        while cur is not None:
            path.append(cur)
            cur = parent.get(cur)
        path.reverse()
        for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
            ra,ca = tl(id2node[a])
            rb,cb = tl(id2node[b])
            if rb>ra: remaining_moves.append('DOWN')
            elif rb<ra: remaining_moves.append('UP')
            elif cb>ca: remaining_moves.append('RIGHT')
            elif cb<ca: remaining_moves.append('LEFT')
        print('remaining moves', remaining_moves)
        break
if remaining_moves:
    action(remaining_moves)
print('level completed?', last_action_result.get('level_completed'))

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Check current state
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
blue = next(n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green = next(n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
print('blue id', blue['id'], 'boundary', blue['boundary'])
print('green id', green['id'], 'boundary', green['boundary'])
# Are they adjacent? Check adjacency list
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_set = set()
for i,j in adj:
    adj_set.add((i,j))
    adj_set.add((j,i))
print('adjacent?', (blue['id'], green['id']) in adj_set)
# Recompute path
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
path_set = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9)
blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue['id'], []) if nid in path_set]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green['id'], []) if nid in path_set]
print('blue neighbors', blue_neighbors)
print('green neighbors', green_neighbors)

def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), min(cols)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_id):
    visited=set()
    queue=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        queue.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while queue:
        nid,d = queue.popleft()
        if nid==target_id:
            return d,parent
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_set and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                queue.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

remaining_moves = []
for t in green_neighbors:
    d,parent = bfs(blue_neighbors, t)
    if d is not None:
        cur = t
        path = []
        while cur is not None:
            path.append(cur)
            cur = parent.get(cur)
        path.reverse()
        for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
            ra,ca = tl(id2node[a])
            rb,cb = tl(id2node[b])
            if rb>ra: remaining_moves.append('DOWN')
            elif rb<ra: remaining_moves.append('UP')
            elif cb>ca: remaining_moves.append('RIGHT')
            elif cb<ca: remaining_moves.append('LEFT')
        print('remaining moves', remaining_moves)
        break
if remaining_moves:
    action(remaining_moves)
print('level completed?', last_action_result.get('level_completed'))

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# New level 2. Inspect board
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
print('level', current_frame.level, 'step', current_frame.step)
# Count objects by color
from collections import Counter
cnt = Counter(n['color'] for n in nodes)
print('color counts', cnt)
# Identify blue, green, red
blue_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b']
green_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N']
red_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R']
print('blue ids', blue_ids, 'green ids', green_ids, 'red ids', red_ids)
# Path nodes? Probably gray/white squares
path_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9]
print('path count', len(path_ids))
# Build adjacency
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
# Find blue neighbors
blue_id = blue_ids[0]
blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
print('blue neighbors', blue_neighbors)
# Green neighbors
green_id = green_ids[0]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
print('green neighbors', green_neighbors)
# Red object?
red_id = red_ids[0]
print('red neighbors', adj_map.get(red_id, []))
# Let's find top-left positions
def tl(n):
    b = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in b]
    cols = [p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), min(cols)
blue_node = next(n for n in nodes if n['id']==blue_id)
print('blue tl', tl(blue_node))
green_node = next(n for n in nodes if n['id']==green_id)
print('green tl', tl(green_node))
red_node = next(n for n in nodes if n['id']==red_id)
print('red tl', tl(red_node))
# Possibly need to move blue to green, but red blocks? Might be a switch?
# Let's see adjacency between red and path
red_path_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(red_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
print('red path neighbors', red_path_neighbors)

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Build path graph and find shortest path from blue to green avoiding red?
# Let's inspect adjacency of path nodes
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)

path_ids = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9)
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
red_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R')

def tl(n):
    b=n['boundary']
    return min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b)

blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
print('blue neighbors', blue_neighbors)
print('green neighbors', green_neighbors)

from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_ids, blocked=None):
    visited=set()
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        q.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    blocked=set(blocked or [])
    while q:
        nid,d = q.popleft()
        if nid in target_ids:
            # reconstruct
            cur=nid
            path=[]
            while cur is not None:
                path.append(cur)
                cur=parent.get(cur)
            path.reverse()
            return d,path
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_ids and nb not in visited and nb not in blocked:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                q.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

# Try without blocking red
d,path = bfs(blue_neighbors, green_neighbors)
print('dist without block', d, path)
# Try blocking red neighbors? Red may be an obstacle occupying a path node?
# Check if red node is on path? red id 11, color R, pixels? Let's see
red_node = id2node[red_id]
print('red node pixels', red_node['pixels'], 'color', red_node['color'])
# Red might be a barrier covering a path node? Let's see adjacency between red and path nodes: red path neighbors [10,12,22]
# Might need to go around red. Let's compute moves.
def moves_from_path(path_nodes):
    moves=[]
    for a,b in zip(path_nodes, path_nodes[1:]):
        ra,ca = tl(id2node[a])
        rb,cb = tl(id2node[b])
        if rb>ra: moves.append('DOWN')
        elif rb<ra: moves.append('UP')
        elif cb>ca: moves.append('RIGHT')
        elif cb<ca: moves.append('LEFT')
    return moves

if d is not None:
    print('moves', moves_from_path(path))
# Execute moves
if d is not None:
    moves = moves_from_path(path)
    print('executing', moves)
    action(moves)

# Let's find path graph from blue to green
from collections import deque
def bfs(start_ids, target_ids):
    visited=set()
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    for s in start_ids:
        q.append((s,0))
        visited.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while q:
        nid,d = q.popleft()
        if nid in target_ids:
            cur=nid
            path=[]
            while cur is not None:
                path.append(cur)
                cur=parent.get(cur)
            path.reverse()
            return d,path
        for nb in adj_map.get(nid, []):
            if nb in path_ids and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=nid
                q.append((nb,d+1))
    return None,None

blue_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(blue_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
d,path = bfs(blue_neighbors, green_neighbors)
print('dist', d, 'path nodes', path)
if d is not None:
    # compute moves
    def tlpos(nid):
        n=id2node[nid]

# Blue is on path node 3 (tl 27,12). Need to get to green at right end.
# The path seems blocked by red at top. Maybe we need to go down the loop under the path to bypass red.
# Let's map path nodes with coordinates and adjacency.
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
def tl(n):
    b=n['boundary']
    return min(p[0] for p in b), min(p[1] for p in b)
path_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9]
adj = seg['adjacency_list']
adj_map = {}
for i,j in adj:
    adj_map.setdefault(i, []).append(j)
    adj_map.setdefault(j, []).append(i)
path_adj = {pid:[n for n in adj_map.get(pid, []) if n in path_ids] for pid in path_ids}
# Find blue's current path node
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
blue_tl = tl(id2node[blue_id])
# Find path node with same tl as blue (overlap)
blue_path_node = None
for pid in path_ids:
    if tl(id2node[pid]) == blue_tl:
        blue_path_node = pid
        break
print('blue on path node', blue_path_node, blue_tl)
# Green neighbor path node
green_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='N')
green_neighbors = [nid for nid in adj_map.get(green_id, []) if nid in path_ids]
print('green neighbors', green_neighbors)
# BFS from blue_path_node to green neighbors via path nodes, but we must consider that blue cannot move through red? Red overlaps path node 10? Let's see which path node red overlaps.
red_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R')
red_bb = (min(p[0] for p in id2node[red_id]['boundary']), max(p[0] for p in id2node[red_id]['boundary']), min(p[1] for p in id2node[red_id]['boundary']), max(p[1] for p in id2node[red_id]['boundary']))
blocked_nodes = []
for pid in path_ids:
    n = id2node[pid]
    bb = (min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']), max(p[0] for p in n['boundary']), min(p[1] for p in n['boundary']), max(p[1] for p in n['boundary']))
    # overlap?
    if not (red_bb[1] < bb[0] or red_bb[0] > bb[1] or red_bb[3] < bb[2] or red_bb[2] > bb[3]):
        blocked_nodes.append(pid)
print('red overlaps path nodes', blocked_nodes)
# Remove blocked nodes from graph
available_nodes = set(path_ids) - set(blocked_nodes)
# BFS
from collections import deque
def bfs(start, targets):
    if start not in available_nodes:
        return None
    visited=set()
    q=deque([(start,[start])])
    visited.add(start)
    while q:
        nid,path = q.popleft()
        if nid in targets:
            return path
        for nb in path_adj.get(nid, []):
            if nb in available_nodes and nb not in visited:
                visited.add(nb)
                q.append((nb, path+[nb]))
    return None
path_to_green = bfs(blue_path_node, green_neighbors)
print('path to green (avoid red)', path_to_green)
if path_to_green:
    moves=[]
    for a,bid in zip(path_to_green, path_to_green[1:]):
        ra,ca = tl(id2node[a])
        rb,cb = tl(id2node[bid])
        if rb>ra: moves.append('DOWN')
        elif rb<ra: moves.append('UP')
        elif cb>ca: moves.append('RIGHT')
        elif cb<ca: moves.append('LEFT')
    print('moves', moves)
    action(moves)
    print('level completed?', last_action_result.get('level_completed'))

# Blue tl 27,12 but blue on path node None. Maybe blue overlaps path node but tl doesn't match because blue is 3x3? Let's compute overlap via bbox intersection.
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
id2node = {n['id']: n for n in nodes}
def bbox(n):
    b=n['boundary']
    rows=[p[0] for p in b]
    cols=[p[1] for p in b]
    return min(rows), max(rows), min(cols), max(cols)
blue_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='b')
blue_bb = bbox(id2node[blue_id])
print('blue bb', blue_bb)
path_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g') and n['pixels']==9]
for pid in path_ids:
    bb = bbox(id2node[pid])
    if not (blue_bb[1] < bb[0] or blue_bb[0] > bb[1] or blue_bb[3] < bb[2] or blue_bb[2] > bb[3]):
        print('overlap path', pid, bb)
# Find which path node blue is on by center?
# Maybe blue is a 3x3 object sitting on top of path node 3, so blue's bbox equals path node's bbox? Let's compare.
for pid in path_ids:
    bb = bbox(id2node[pid])
    if bb == blue_bb:
        print('exact match', pid)
# If not exact, maybe blue is offset.
# Let's list path nodes around (27,12)
for pid in path_ids:
    bb = bbox(id2node[pid])
    if bb[0]==27 and bb[2]==12:
        print('path at 27,12', pid, bb)

Read transition metadata from fields/keys such as `last_action_result['board_changed']`, `last_action_result['done']`, `last_action_result['level_completed']`, `last_action_result['game_over']`, `last_action_result['reward']`, and `last_action_result['valid_actions']`.
- `valid_actions` is the current list of valid action names.
- Call `action(actions)` to execute one or more real environment actions from Python.
- Pass `action(actions)` a list like `['LEFT']` or `[{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 7}]`.
- One action usually returns one frame, but a single action can result in a short multi-frame animation.
- After `action(actions)` returns, `current_frame`, `previous_frame`, `history`, `transitions`, `valid_actions`, and `last_action_result` are refreshed.
- Each result reports `board_changed`, plus `gameplay_changed` and `no_impact`: the harness learns the game's deterministic HUD/edge band (a moves-remaining or timer bar) online and tells you whether your action changed real gameplay (`gameplay_changed`) or only advanced that band (`no_impact` -- a wasted move, e.g. pressing into a wall). `hud_band` names the learned band when one exists (e.g. `rows 61-62`).
- `action(actions, intent=...)` defaults to `intent='explore'`: an explore action that turns out `no_impact` STOPS the rest of that batch (`stop_reason='no_impact_action'`) and returns so you re-ground, instead of wasting the queued actions on a plan the environment just disproved. Pass `intent='solve'` for a committed sequence you do not want interrupted by the no-impact check.
- Optional precision upgrade for that check: if you can pin down the deterministic HUD/bar exactly, write a PURE `advance_hud(frame, action) -> frame` (frame is the `.ascii` letter grid; return it with ONLY the bar advanced one step, everything else identical) and commit it in a `HUD model:` section with a fenced python code block. The harness re-verifies it against every action and, while its bar prediction holds, uses it (`no_impact_source: model`) instead of the statistical band -- you write it ONCE and it then runs free every turn with no further tokens. It only asks you to rewrite when it mispredicts (`hud_model: stale`, e.g. a refill or a new level). No HUD in this game? Don't write one -- the statistical fallback handles it (`no_impact_source: band` or `exact`).
- `ACTION7` is a valid game-specific action when it appears in `valid_actions`. Its meaning is not fixed across games; infer it from a safe probe and the returned before/after and animation metadata rather than assuming it means undo, confirm, or back.
- Every action in the result's `executed_actions` carries an `animation` record summarizing its intermediate frames (which are not visible in `current_frame`): `num_frames`, `changed`, `only_changed` (a transient flash that left the same final board), `total_cells_changed`, `cells_changed_per_frame` (per frame, where 0 is a held/dwell frame), and `objects` -- one string per connected animated region, e.g. `top-left (19,27) 4x4, 16 cells, per-frame [...]`, so two things moving at once (a box resizing while a light blinks) each keep a tight bounding box.
- Beyond the `animation` record above, two optional runtime variables expose the actual per-action frames: `last_animation` and `frame_stats`.
- `current_frame` is always the settled board after your last action -- on its own it is enough for a purely static reading, and you never have to look further.
- If you want to, `last_animation` additionally exposes every frame the engine produced for each INDIVIDUAL action of your most recent `action(...)` call: a list with one entry per action, in execution order, each with `.action` and `.frames` (intermediate animation frames plus the final frame; length 1 means that action caused no animation). After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.

Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.

Motion may be meaningful (an object sliding, a chain reaction, a knock-on effect) OR incidental (a decorative transition, a flashing timer/HUD, a cosmetic redraw). Treat multi-frame motion as a HYPOTHESIS to test against the puzzle, not a fact. Reading `last_animation` costs tokens only when you inspect it, so pull it only when you expect it to help.
